name: Bitcoin
day_summary: Bitcoin rose 1.26% on Sunday to $65,330 — breaching the $65,000 buy-trigger threshold named in Saturday's dossier — after a two-phase session: 21 hours of tight $63,682–$64,672 consolidation with the 200-DMA zone holding as intraday support (low: $63,683), then a late-session volume surge at 21:00 UTC (275 BTC in one hour, ~4× the day's hourly pace) that vaulted BTC to a session high of $65,479. The short-term holder realized price (~$65,000) has been reclaimed. FOMC is three days away; the evidence stack is the strongest it has been at any point in the June correction.

short_pnl: −1.26% — bears squeezed on two counts: the 200-DMA zone held for a second straight session and the $65K resistance that anchored short positioning has been broken; FOMC in three days tightens the risk window further

decision.rationale: Upgrading to HIGH conviction BUY. The $65,000 level explicitly named as the buy-confirmation trigger in Saturday's dossier has been breached: BTC spiked to $65,479 intraday and is holding $65,330 at the close of US-hours trading. The evidence stack now has five pillars: (1) $65K trigger hit — the short-term holder realized price (~$65,000) has been reclaimed, structurally reducing selling pressure as recent buyers move back into profit; (2) 200-DMA zone ($63,500–$63,600) held for the second consecutive session (today's low $63,683), cementing the resistance-to-support flip; (3) ETF inflow reversal confirmed — all 13 US spot BTC ETFs posted $85.85M in net inflows on June 12, ending the 13-session, $4.4B outflow streak; (4) FOMC June 17 at 98.2% probability of no rate change, near-zero perp funding, and Fear & Greed at 21 (Extreme Fear) — the most asymmetric FOMC setup of the cycle; (5) Galaxy Digital's bearish cycle targets ($40K–$54K) are being actively invalidated by price action. Primary caveat: Sunday volume (~$100M on Crypto.com vs. $29B+ weekday norms) means the $65K break is not institutionally confirmed until Monday ETF flow data validates it. Stop: $59,480 (June 6 capitulation wick). Add in the $65,300–$65,500 zone. Targets: $67,520 (June 3 swing high) → $70,000 (round number) → $75,500 (June 27 options max pain, ~$8B notional).

what_traders_are_doing: Heading into the most consequential FOMC of the year with Bitcoin above the key $65,000 level for the first time since the June correction began. Sunday's session split into two distinct phases: passive, range-bound positioning through most of the day as BTC consolidated between $63,682 and $64,672 — the 200-DMA zone absorbing the intraday dip for a second consecutive session — followed by an abrupt $1,480 rally compressed into the 21:00 UTC hour (275 BTC, roughly 4× the day's preceding hourly average). The thesis laid out in Saturday's dossier has materially advanced: ETF inflows reversed on June 12 ($85.85M, ending the 13-session bleed), the 200-DMA zone is holding as support for two straight sessions, and $65K has been breached. The positioning setup is as clean as it has been all cycle: perp funding near zero (no crowded longs to flush), Fear & Greed at 21 (maximum contrarian buy signal), and ~$8B in June 27 options notional with max pain at $75,500 pulling 15.6% above current levels. Monday's ETF flow data and Tuesday's pre-FOMC positioning are the next decision points. Galaxy Digital's bear scenario ($40K–$54K) requires FOMC to deliver a hawkish shock — an event CME is pricing at under 2% probability.

analysis:
## $65K breached — trigger confirmed, FOMC in three days

Sunday, June 14: Bitcoin rose 1.26% to $65,330 in a session that delivered exactly the setup the prior dossier called for, then added a late-session exclamation point. For 21 hours, price moved in a narrow $63,682–$64,672 band, consolidating Friday's gain and testing the 200-DMA zone intraday (low: $63,683) without closing below it. Then, at 21:00 UTC, a single candle changed the picture entirely: 275 BTC traded in 60 minutes — roughly 4× the preceding hourly average — driving BTC from $64,013 to $65,290 (a $1,277 intra-hour move) and setting the day's high at $65,479. At $65,330 heading into the final two hours of the UTC day, the stated buy-confirmation trigger has been hit. Three days from FOMC. The question shifts from whether to buy to whether the Sunday move holds.

## Technical analysis

**Trend read.** Bitcoin has built a sequence of higher lows since the June 6 capitulation wick at $59,480: $60,730–$61,509 (June 10–11 shelf), $62,833 (June 12 low), $63,415 (June 13 intraday low), $63,683 (June 14 intraday low). Today's session extended that sequence above the 200-DMA zone for two consecutive sessions for the first time in the June correction. The primary trend since the $98,600 peak in early 2026 remains a corrective downtrend — but the early-reversal signals are accumulating: 200-DMA zone holding as support, ETF inflows restored, and the STH realized price reclaimed intraday.

**Momentum.** RSI is recovering from deeply oversold conditions at the June 5–6 trough, estimated in the 43–48 range heading into this week — approaching the neutral 50 line but not yet overbought. The MACD histogram is compressing toward a potential bullish cross. The 8-session pattern since June 5 is a textbook coiling base: higher lows, declining daily volatility through the $63,500–$64,700 range, and then today's high-volume candle as the first impulse out of the coil. That pattern resolves either up (FOMC cooperates) or down (FOMC surprises hawkish).

**Volume — the most important context for today's session.** The hourly candle breakdown tells two different stories. For 20 consecutive hours (00:00–20:00 UTC), BTC traded 18–113 BTC/hour — typical Sunday volumes on a single exchange, representing perhaps 1/3 of normal weekday flow. The session was quiet, deliberate, and range-bound. Then the 21:00 UTC candle: 275 BTC / $18M in 60 minutes. That single candle's volume exceeded the combined volume of the six preceding hours. Three interpretations: (a) an institutional player initiating a pre-FOMC position; (b) stop-liquidation of short sellers clustered at the $65K level; or (c) a combination of both (the stops create the liquidity, the buyer absorbs it). All three explanations are bullish in structure — but none constitutes the same confirmation as a sustained multi-hour buy program on Monday weekday volume with ETF flows confirming. The $65K break is real. Whether it is validated is Monday's job.

**★ Strongest resistance: $65,479 — today's session high + STH realized price cluster.** This level concentrates three independent forces: (1) the short-term holder realized price is approximately $65,000, meaning wallets that bought BTC in the past 155 days have their cost basis here — breaching and holding above this level moves that cohort from loss to profit and reduces their incentive to sell; (2) Deribit's $65,000 call strike carries some of the heaviest open interest on the June expiry, meaning dealer delta-hedging creates a mechanical bid as spot approaches from below and a mechanical ceiling as it approaches from above (until the strike is decisively cleared); (3) today's intraday high of $65,479 is the first resistance — a Monday open above $65,479 on volume confirms the Sunday spike was not a fakeout but rather a pre-FOMC accumulation move. The ★ designation is on this level specifically because it is the near-term confirmation gate: above it means the bull thesis is intact and growing; a fakeout below $65,000 resets the picture.

**★ Strongest support: $63,500–$63,600 — the 200-DMA zone.** The evidence: June 13 intraday low of $63,415 (2.9 hours of trading below the zone before recovering); June 14 intraday low of $63,683 (holding above the zone entirely, no close below). Two consecutive sessions of testing the 200-DMA and bouncing. Former resistance for three sessions (June 10–12) has now flipped to support on two tests. The zone is bolstered by the 200-day moving average — a level watched by every systematic fund, risk-model overlay, and macro participant in the market. A daily close below $63,500 before FOMC would be the warning: it would mean the resistance-to-support flip has failed and BTC has re-entered the 200-DMA zone from above, materially increasing the probability that FOMC volatility tests the June 6 low.

**The FOMC setup.** Three days from now, Kevin Warsh delivers his first FOMC decision, dot plot, and press conference. CME FedWatch: 98.2% probability of hold at 3.50%–3.75%. The base case — a hold with a dot plot that doesn't introduce a hike signal — is nearly fully priced in the rates market but not in Bitcoin. With perp funding near zero, Fear & Greed at 21, and short sellers squeezed off the 200-DMA over two sessions, the crowd is positioned defensively. A neutral FOMC hold — what markets expect — is the catalyst for a positioning unwind that pushes BTC toward $67,520 in the first post-decision hours. The tail risk is a hawkish surprise in the dot plot or Warsh's press conference language — a scenario Goldman Sachs has flagged (no rate cuts in 2026) that, if confirmed officially, cracks $59,480 and opens the Galaxy Digital bear scenario.

**Decision points.** (1) Monday open: does BTC hold above $65,000 or fade back below the STH realized price? A Monday open above $65,000 with the first hour holding confirms the Sunday move. (2) Monday ETF flows: second consecutive net-inflow day validates the June 12 reversal as a trend, not a one-day anomaly. (3) Pre-FOMC close Tuesday: where is BTC positioned heading into Wednesday's binary? Above $65K is the best-case setup for a non-hawkish squeeze. (4) FOMC outcome Wednesday: the trade is on or the stop is triggered.

**What invalidates the read.** A confirmed daily close below $63,500 (200-DMA zone) before FOMC — not an intraday wick, but a close — would mean the $65K spike was a bull trap and the corrective structure is reasserting. Below $59,480, every target discussed in this dossier is void and the Galaxy bear scenario must be entertained seriously.
